heading: `exclusive` — rules that must not both fire
text:
### `exclusive` — rules that must not both fire [LTSL.8.8]

`exclusive <rule>, <rule>[, …]` asserts that **no two of the named rules fire
within the same pump**, for every pump in the scenario.

It names at least two rules; one is a compile error. Rule names are bound
against the program's rule inventory as `activated` binds them ([LTSL.8.2]), so
a misspelled rule fails to compile rather than passing vacuously. With more
than two names the assertion is **pairwise**: no two of the set may share a
pump.

**The scope is the pump.** A pump runs to quiescence, so rules that fire in one
pump are treated as responding to the same input regardless of which fact
triggered each. Scoping co-firing to rules that matched a common fact instead
would make two rules that both match a long-lived configuration fact never
exclusive, which is a silent false pass. A pump that batches unrelated inputs produces a false FAILURE
instead, and a test that wrongly fails is investigated.

The surface carries no scope selector. If a narrower one is ever needed it is a
new form, not a modifier on this one.

```{admonition} This is an observation, not a proof
:class: warning
`exclusive` holds when no co-firing was OBSERVED in the scenarios that ran. It
is not a statement that the rules are mutually exclusive by construction — a
dynamic test can only sample. An author who means "these can never both fire"
is making a claim about the rules' conditions, which this assertion does not
check and does not attempt to.
```

`never exclusive …` is not admitted. The inverse — asserting that two rules DO
co-fire — has not been asked for, and reserving the spelling costs nothing.
